It's Eileen Laubacher, the Democrat and retired U.S. Navy Rear Admiral running against Lauren Boebert here in Colorado.
I was 17-years-old the first time I raised my right hand and took an oath to support and defend the Constitution against all enemies, foreign and domestic.
I took those words, and that responsibility, seriously every day for the next 4 decades. When I was an intelligence officer. When I was deployed to Afghanistan. When I became an Admiral. And as a member of the president’s National Security Council.
But in all those years, I have never felt as much of a threat to our country, our Constitution, and our very democracy as I do right now. I said I would never run for office. But in this moment, I feel an obligation to step up, serve my community, and defend our country once again.
I am running for Congress to defeat Lauren Boebert because when she was sworn into office, Lauren took a similar oath to defend our Constitution – and she has betrayed it almost every single day since then.
Adam Frisch only lost to Lauren Boebert by 546 votes. It was the closest race in the entire country. We can finally put an end to Lauren Boebert’s embarrassing political career – but I need your help now to do it.

TO: U.S. Postal Service
FROM: Willis
Subject: Please don’t cave to Trump.

Dear USPS,

**I am writing today to DEMAND that you stand up to Donald Trump and PROTECT vote-by-mail.**

Vote-by-mail has expanded voting access to millions of Americans in rural areas, serving overseas, and in marginalized communities.

Limiting access to states who do Trump’s bidding is UNDEMOCRATIC and straight up AUTHORITARIAN!

The Postal Service is a vital institution that has done so much good for our country — **so please don’t sacrifice everything you stand for now.**

[I’m signing this letter today to DEMAND you stand up to Trump and this disgusting attack on voting rights. subject: This number is bothering me
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Seth for Massachusetts
body:
Hey,
I wanted to check in one more time before tonight’s deadline.
We’re $1,482 away from hitting our mid-month goal.
With Election Day this close, that number matters. What we raise tonight is money we can directly put to work before voters make their choice.

subject: In almost 250 years, there’s never been a Native woman serving in the US Senate.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR AND AUTHORIZED BY DEB FOR NEW MEXICO**
body:
| | |
---
[](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15971?refcode=jtk1221-bu-nd&t=1&akid=11728%2E400544%2EjuvDC9)
Friend, in almost 250 years, there’s never been a Native woman serving in the US Senate. **It’s time to change that.**

I’m Peggy Flanagan, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Minnesota.
I am Ojibwe and a proud member of the White Earth Nation. My family is the Wolf Clan. The mission of my clan is to never leave anyone behind — and that’s been my guiding principle.

I am the descendant of people who were forced off their land onto the White Earth reservation. I am the relative of residential boarding school survivors. I am the daughter of a man who always spoke truth to power for the good of the Anishinaabe people.

I’m thinking of my daughter — who just got her first jingle dress — and whether or not she will see Indigenous women in all parts of our government.
**Right now, there are _no_ Native voices in the US Senate. _If I win this race, we can change that._**

**[It's high time that all our communities have a seat at the table. If you agree, will you pitch in $10 or whatever you can to power my campaign and Deb Haaland’s and help me make history?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15971?refcode=jtk1221-bu-nd&t=2&akid=11728%2E400544%2EjuvDC9)**
| | [Donate](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15971?refcode=jtk1221-bu-nd&t=3&akid=11728%2E400544%2EjuvDC9)
---
Too often, Native voices are ignored or erased in the halls of power.

That’s how we get awful so-called leaders like Donald Trump and J.D. Vance, who called Indigenous Peoples' Day a “fake holiday” and said that Native land was “enemy territory.”

My Ojibwe name means "Speaks in a Loud and Clear Voice woman." So I’m using that voice to call out MAGA extremism — loudly and clearly.
But I can’t do it alone. I need your help to build a campaign strong enough to cut through the noise. **[That’s why I’m personally asking, friend, will you pitch in a split gift to my campaign to help us make history?](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/15971?refcode=jtk1221-bu-nd&t=4&akid=11728%2E400544%2EjuvDC9)**

Six years later, he's still pushing the lie | | | | Derek, I'm the official Democratic nominee for Governor of Wisconsin, and I need to tell you something about my opponent that should alarm you no matter where you live. **Tom Tiffany still pushes debunked conspiracy theories claiming the 2020 election was rigged, even after that result has been confirmed over and over by recounts, audits, and court rulings in state after state.** And it's not just talk: Tiffany supports rewarding the people behind that lie, going so far as to suggest insurrectionists who stormed the Capitol should receive taxpayer-funded restitution. Think about that. Money out of your pocket, funneled to people who attacked our democracy, because a Republican in Congress won't accept that he lost. **Is this the guy we want appointing the people who oversee Wisconsin's pivotal electoral votes?** This isn't even a fringe position for Tiffany. From abortion bans to cutting food assistance, he's as extreme as they come. **[We cannot let an election denier take control of how Wisconsin runs its elections. clean_body: Six years later, he's still pushing the lie | | | | Derek, I'm the official Democratic nominee for Governor of Wisconsin, and I need to tell you something about my opponent that should alarm you no matter where you live. Tom Tiffany still pushes debunked conspiracy theories claiming the 2020 election was rigged, even after that result has been confirmed over and over by recounts, audits, and court rulings in state after state. And it's not just talk: Tiffany supports rewarding the people behind that lie, going so far as to suggest insurrectionists who stormed the Capitol should receive taxpayer-funded restitution. Think about that. Money out of your pocket, funneled to people who attacked our democracy, because a Republican in Congress won't accept that he lost. Is this the guy we want appointing the people who oversee Wisconsin's pivotal electoral votes? This isn't even a fringe position for Tiffany. ##### **SITREP-02**
On July 27, 2026, at the Sumter County Republican Club meeting in Sumterville, a voter asked which of the three candidates present live in District 11.
Wilkins spoke for Strada. He spoke for Baker. Neither of them were present. He decided who lives in the district and who doesn't.
He joked that Baker doesn't get his mailers because Baker doesn't live in the district.
Then he said: "I'm pretty sure that we live in the district, right Ivette."
I confirmed I do--contrary to his misrepresentation on his website.
When I called it out, he said: "We don't want to go there, Ivette. I like you."
Asked directly, he admitted: "I live in the district as well."
As well. Meaning: in addition to me.
He acknowledged it on camera. In front of witnesses. Twice.
Then he sent a mailer to our district claiming--on both sides--that he is "The ONLY Candidate who lives in Our District." See the copy I received below.

name: Abdul El-Sayed
subject: I can’t stop thinking about this
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
I know it's late, but my mind is racing thinking about these Senate Leadership Fund ads.
Peter,
I know it's late, but my mind is racing thinking about these Senate Leadership Fund ads — called “SLF” for short.
SLF is a Super PAC with a sole focus on electing Republicans to the Senate. **By Election Day, they will have spent $51 million — possibly more — on Michigan alone.**
Just like the $70 million we were up against in the primary, it’s hard to even fathom that amount of money.
But despite how scary that sounds, I still believe we’re going to win in November. Here’s why:
The Senate Leadership Fund has run this playbook before, in races just like ours. It spends millions trying to bury campaigns that won't play by its rules — and in almost every one of those races, one of two scenarios plays out:
1. When a campaign has the resources to tell its own story and break through the noise, SLF's ads don't land.
2. When a campaign runs dry, gets overwhelmed, and can't respond, that's when the ads seal their fate.

So the honest answer to whether we get to defy the odds once again in November isn't complicated. **It comes down to whether we have enough grassroots power to keep running our own ads, reaching our own voters, and holding onto our story before SLF defines it for us.**
Peter, I fully trust that our team has what it takes to out-maneuver and out-organize $51+ million. I've put my faith in you since the very beginning, and you've never let me down.
**I wouldn't be writing to you this late if I didn't believe what you do tonight matters to what happens in this race.** So please, if you can pitch in $5 or any amount so we can keep our ads on the air and our story in our own hands, it would make a real difference. Can I count on your support?
[**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-ms-aes-20260815-3-ak**](https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260815-3-ak.OKq3hn&amount=5&refcode=em20260815-2930&t=2&akid=2941%2E251025%2EEnqV1N)
Thank you, truly.
Abdul

Peter, in almost 250 years, there’s never been a Native woman serving in the US Senate. **It’s time to change that. ** I’m Peggy Flanagan, the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Minnesota. I am Ojibwe and a proud member of the White Earth Nation. My family is the Wolf Clan. The mission of my clan is to never leave anyone behind — and that’s been my guiding principle. I am the descendant of people who were forced off their land onto the White Earth reservation. I am the relative of residential boarding school survivors. I am the daughter of a man who always spoke truth to power for the good of the Anishinaabe people. I’m thinking of my daughter — who just got her first jingle dress — and whether or not she will see Indigenous women in all parts of our government. **Right now, there are**** _no_****Native voices in the US Senate.****_If I win this race, we can change that. _** [**It's high time that all our communities have a seat at the table. If you agree, will you pitch in $10 or whatever you can to power my campaign and Rep. Zoe Lofgren****’s****and help me make history?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/137316851/640397958/2095829082?amount=10&refcode=EM_ALL_ZOL_FRS_1_2026-08-15_PFG_SPL_ES-56517&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDMvMS82OTYwNiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1MjNlYTMxZS0yMDk5LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDBkM2ExMWZhMzAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=II_cCS4OB6yP_S2TNcC82EbTvZvczLUtHhAKFgq6Ikc=)

Too often, Native voices are ignored or erased in the halls of power. That’s how we get awful so-called leaders like Donald Trump and J.D. A resurfaced 2010 video from Promsex's own YouTube account shows she was leading half-naked participants, including men dressed in women's clothing, on parade through the streets of Lima.

Scientists say your dinnertime could be shaping your blood sugar, your cravings, and even your heart health, and the growing field of chrononutrition finds that eating at the wrong hour can throw off the body's internal clock. Poorer blood sugar control. Stronger cravings the next day. Even a higher risk of heart disease. ## Violent Crime Posts Record One-Year Drop
Violent crime in the U.S. posted its [largest one-year drop](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGutCAUhJ8GOwwgohYUf2O3f3tLw8phPTcoGzgruW9_42bf4HaTmWQm33zdlpvDiMfjv9vBUkjLAbVEIIK8nJgiHLRm3MGnerhC6UUhp0UJZbgYuTSLWwlPWLRrvA0ACroGrBxGMw7aTKLZrOgnP0ihRymDdhOsvQcXeh30MIXe6Qbt1SdGaaQQWo-tcb1UHlTX9QYCrEwL8Egpt98JD9ogxJ90Qm7XtDfRbkTPwrp_TM1MzbXWdr2Xi-PKmZovydQc7sjfLNw7cvxD97H2V_aQed2QgG_pVYCpucnWPyvGiMUMTIvH7jC-R-mPX51W_QYAAP__XbuA3w) on record in 2025, with murders down 18.1%, robberies down 18.5%, and aggravated assaults down 7.2%, according to the FBI's annual report released on Friday. The homicide rate of [4.1 per 100,000](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O6yAUhJ_G7ogAY34Kituky223tDAc4rPCxsInjvbtV84rbDkaaTTf9_WYHgELbs__YQVPuU4bvI8CRNCmE2uBjWLDFVJ9b-Gg-qLc6iS51IxbJvQUIuEJkwp98hlAwtCDF8Zqa5R2vF-8G000fATuBpm40wK0zTZJM5usjZI9-muPW6EF50rZmw6jkAnkMIwaMsROcUhItd2-K260QC4_9YR2i3Xti1-I9qMb_nXy3sl72C-Eq7pCI4wFOnlf6ooRE7AEsUE4gFF7rTv70LEWCA6WZ2QuOTBuno0QRgXNVVRh5toGba2JVvbNp_2NpeChTaf4cw1YPkfoj_5OL38DAAD__69MhFg) people is tied with 1955 and 1956 as the lowest since 1900. President Trump credited his administration's [crime-fighting policies](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGupCAUhp8GOyZ4QAYLim3o7rZbGq4cRzYIBo6a-_YbJ_MGW__Jl__7_nxNXz6mmF-__YaWljJlvFpCIqzTGUvCTHONG4ZyZd-oHLTUMoEAzYXhvZ78TPHESfku2AURUHZo-6fR5qn0KLrVjlKZwWAQ0sPo1QAQjBwhfEuQi-hlF-3NE6bXvRBKmYf2Qw8BQcpB44IzUwJDpFIff0vMtOKSfsqJ9TGXrUt2Jdobk78YOAYu_-yl0T0xcDeYgROGgesVA3c0fhsycFSPbedHPjGmxpfvyN-ivOJeKvG2livmF_9E-Iyhlp174hXnUgOvnpCB66oN-xVTik0_mRKvzcf0Pkf_2fS08C8AAP__JLGMjA), including a crackdown on criminal migrants, fewer illegal border crossings, and National Guard deployments to cities like Washington, D.C. Early data show declines continuing through the first half of 2026, pointing to another historic low.
## Trump Makes Claim on Strait of Hormuz
President Trump claimed on Friday that he will soon [make the Strait of Hormuz a U.S. territory.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQRp_GdI6MMWOncLENXbbdEnlhCLPyT2QPRNmnv-K-wq2P9B19589jfgSKlJ-_Q0LPW5kzvltEZqzzSSVi5qVSwrW8c2hcDt5qmbXSIJWTPcxhYTpxNqFb_YaocejQ99aBswbuqts92BHvMP4dRzeYOxg3WGdxXZQK4CwuHflrT7keeqWMcTcIY69X1MMwAm64CKNwJS719q9Q5h23-Ckn1ttSUhf9zvxqYvgl9CT0xDvuFOPFhJ72kvC6JPQU1kSZGtfAVLLQE6hBge0l1yO9ZAufJi9KLMsm91LT8V8eTTLWesk_Qk9d9evrTTFSAyuMeqZA36qOf1jv9PorAAD__6p_hlE) Trump did not elaborate on how he would make the critical shipping lane a U.S. territory, considering that Iran and Oman share jurisdiction. Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi [said on Saturday](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykULuOpDAQ_BrIjIwNDQQOLplsLr0Qeexm8MjYo3YDmvv6Fav9g41KqpLq9e8-322IIT3_2g0NL3lOeJaIzEjzEXLExI7Chj6fyRbOOy-UZyUVCDmKFmbrOBw4d7b2ZkFUqGs07TDCOHQwyXo1TuKgwE4aOtReTpN0HnqrUavpAbKvg7n85NhCK2XXjQ3YvlUeldY94IKu6iT6wJmaVw6JV1ziJx9IjctbHc3K_C6V_lOpW6Vu53k26eGuHZd-MZmir9QtkE0_IAhf6LgIj3EvIacimPbtLQqTDSzWTNv-X-xFMBJd0R9BLtl-UgBQk_HvM8QYCgxVJ5-bDfG7DP_yw8OorwAAAP__tHSJmA) that the waterway "cannot be seized with a tweet, nor with an aircraft carrier, nor by issuing an order, nor through an election speech." With the price of a gallon of gasoline up 29% from a year earlier, [Trump told a New York audience](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD3OpDAQRE8DGch_GCZwsAnZbLohapk27pWNkekBze1X7BW-7Ekllaren_fyBkq0b78ho-NQlh3vMyEz1uWiknBnXynjWu4dTi4fDrUsSijbiamTdgHPdOFioF1dQFSoW3RynOw0GvsSbXTByikMiEaC1cGOOIzwAm9hBJAoVUvu6ROTtFIIY6bewiDVikrrwWJA3xiBK3Gp_d9CO0cM6VsurL0vuU0uMh9no381am7UfN93_4VYypM2an4ONWo-SiIm_yBUJp_wQa6ffHSfuuHZQcZKHvazA-_x4C7SFrF2SujBaCtlHzmntrr1uCklOu3YGLFloPR_CP_Q3-XUvwAAAP__pb6HRw) that paying "a tiny little bit more for your gasoline" is worth the cost of ensuring "a very evil country" could not have a nuclear weapon.
## Professor in Plagiarism Scandal Found Dead
Jason Arday, the former University of Cambridge professor at the center of a plagiarism scandal, [was found dead](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL8GMo-MMQYCB5dMtpdeiHrcbaZ3jY1sA7d_f2J_4dJ6Uqnq_flYPoADx_U3bGSrT0ukqwSqlfJycgoUq8u8EaYrQqnpqD6nRUllhJxEZxZwlU9aNLRoPZGiviXbjZOZRm1m2b4t9qTVpMEN8oV6HGfvnepn44YBx1kNLdu7T06d6aTUenoYGDqFpPp-MOTJNVoSck358Zk41jf58J1Oyg-XtjbYd617afpfjXo26nld1yO-3P3j5neScsBGPY_IlVB8cVzxB3xCSVFARvgW9Fc42F6ZcSWx5-SplJQFOHcUQrEHWBkyl034dEQUSIDiIvoS2UUYZmU602aL-8UhcDFjo-W6AYefkfU_3Z5W_QsAAP__QlCSRA) in London on Friday, one week after the university announced an investigation into his academic and professional qualifications. Metropolitan police said the death was "unexpected, but is not believed to be suspicious." Arday's appointment in 2023 received massive media attention, much of it celebrating the hiring of [the youngest black professor](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu3CAQRb_G7rAA25hXUKRx99KmtGZh8E6EwYJZe_P30eYXUl_p6pzz63v7BkqU959woONYtox3S8iMdbuoJMzsKx0Yyp2hcXlxrGXTUhshrVBmA8904TZBH1xE1Dj26NRijV0m8yX7p1NK6tk85Ky_1Oy9jzYuQSlj42Ix6KUn9_mTVhkl5TTZwcCsdEA9jrPBiL6bJAbiUoffhTI_MaY_5cI6-HL0yT2Zz9aNPzq9dnq973uI5f3x-OydXg8MBJ1e8S08HI9KYUdx1hKxtVJFLK8cREAIAiJjFWeCnaBSO0TzkAMkkTAIeNTXyaJioz0DU8l9deG8KSVqZukmuR9A6R8U_2fLy-m_AQAA__9rC416) at the university. But his story came under recent scrutiny, including claims that he plagiarized parts of his Ph.D. dissertation and that he once ran 30 marathons in 35 days to raise money for charity. His [death prompted outcries](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOwyAURE9jd0SA8ccuKLZJl223tD7wiYkwRJg4yu1X3itsORppNO_93JYbxhTz_Rs3Mi2UJdN7T9Qa1eWIJVFursaNfHln3Ft5tVDLIrkExicmYEHX4kGLwt6bQCRp6MkIPcGkFcy8X40AIbX2RDoEOwQPcxgBuKdRWxnI9tGce3wSIDhXaroAjkJ6ksMwAgVyneLkYyv18igxt5VC-pSD6sWVrU9mbe25d8NXJ6-dvOLzRDirM9QWXaJOXm2NDWNmD9xLZlg9fpjDzdbo78Q8YVuZfdW84sbsTFLB4BCs0grdzJ0DMQN5gEkOU1-Nf75jSnEH3Sl-3zCmvzPtnw4PI38DAAD__1-zh10) that the allegations were motivated by racism as well as hostility toward DEI policies at universities and other institutions.

**Whatever happened to _Parade Magazine_?** If you grew up in a household that got the Sunday paper, you knew _Parade_. It was right there between the comics and the coupons, a slim, glossy magazine you never subscribed to but never missed. And for decades, it was one of the most widely read publications. Marshall Field III, the department store heir, launched _Parade_ in 1941 as a picture-heavy Sunday supplement for his _Chicago Sun_ and a handful of other papers. By the late 1980s, it was tucked inside more than 330 newspapers, boasting a circulation north of 35 million and a readership that topped 80 million. Here's a gallery of [Parade's own favorite covers.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAURb8Gb47wMwY8MHTxlq4drRd4JFTYRPDqqP36Kq3UH-h475XOlc7beT1jymm_vuJGjmNZd3q0TMxU1yOVTDv7mjYK5bFj4_LBsZYVJOhe2n7QK3pOB60Ku-AiEdDYkRuM1dYoPcvu5sBID2MMpC4RJpjlxcY5Is5xsgb83CX35Ek76EFKpexJ4zRAIBjHSVMkL5SkkLjU03tJO98o5s9yUD35snXZ3ZjvTYwvAhYByx0rBnpOApYBjFFS_tUClgs17n9Tv-EVv9JOvX_imoClqy7cHynn1LQRSl43TPnnh_-p53DwHQAA___-rnov) Its features became Sunday morning rituals. _[Walter Scott's Personality Parade](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkrGO2zwQhJ-G6mwsd0mKLFTcD8Pd_U0QpBQoanVmjhINiZbgtw8kHwKkSpFmOJgPHCyJ_fHevvuY4vTxvx-5KUNuJ96WxKXw3K4xJ55KmOPIfd4mv5T8KMOcWwQ0J7AnaVofSly5Vb7qm4EZmSpuZG2NrZVxUN2agbpOA4DVSL3qgwQbeqOpMxI654YqNnsfWGkkgFL2bLyW2DMSacMDB6GA-1jyfP6Z41RuPKRnXnk-hzxWqbmVcl8EvQm8Crxu23bmzj93KPAay65YWyRLZFApQdf2kQRdvn8TaMZPXougizx8iP1vPx--lvKkCQFO0qHWJxBogh_vB9RETkqFuKcl5_S6DgB7RXgsJY9HxJ1ATW8vXcflOL_C-6F_TIia_gNWTvqOOolODs47hlBDYD242tbYCzQph_Z-ey4x-NSOi6CLM5bcF4lT4ZmX8iL7k5aQPo9x_tZdzU1_32JKcTG1UPAx-piO3y7_uCRrg78CAAD__yLtv8A)_ , the celebrity Q&A column on the inside cover, was written for 33 years by Lloyd Shearer under that pen name, and was arguably the most widely read column in America. The annual [_What People Earn_ issue,](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D1uwzAMxfHT2FsM6otRBg1dsqVrR0OxqISFbAU2ayG3L9wrdHnLA37D_-s23iIXXh6fcaYguY4Lta2QCK3jzrXQItPKM6XalrhJ_ZG81lGDxhP4k8IxTsI7jTb2KWQiTaanoM4e_dniBfpnSBkh5ZwmR6AvzpDzd7qbZL13zlvbczg88AoVgLV-wOiUTqSNcUiZps4CJZa6Dt-VF3lSLu-60zpMde5LeIq8ts58dPra6WtrbaB7fB9np68sxxrtUAMgKgX9GtKrcSm84bmz8Jgjlz9K_llgD_o3AAD__5q2bxg) which ran for four decades, let you peek at your neighbor's salary alongside Hollywood's. And the [_Parade_ All-America High School Football Team](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFurDAQRb_GdEb2AAYKF6-h29emRBN7WBwZbNmzoPx9tPmF9Ff36JyPx_rAEMP5_I8HWd7SetJdIzFTWa-QIp3sSjjIp_vEyunFW0krKDBSTVKbFR2Hi9YeG283IqCuIavHyUxjb2bV7NYZB37Uxn2OXQ9qRL_5eSb0atpmNFMT7PtPTdpopfp-ag0OGjxB1w2GNnKiV-QDp9J-pXDyTlv8TheV1qWjiXZnzlV0_wQsApb7vtu3RMZMpb4nAhYsHFwkAUtlGdMrVJlTZelDzchul3o2ncxY0JPEGAUsxgygh1nA0hTr8x1iDNWMolfPA0P8ZfMfk10WfgIAAP__fo2Bfg), launched in 1963, proved uncannily prophetic--its alumni include Joe Montana, Peyton Manning, and 14 future Heisman Trophy winners. _Parade_ even nudged history. In 1960, editor Jess Gorkin published an open letter to President Dwight Eisenhower and Soviet Premier Nikita Khrushchev, urging a direct crisis phone link, asking, "_Must a world be lost for want of a telephone call_?" After the Cuban Missile Crisis exposed just how dangerously slow superpower communication was, the Washington-Moscow hotline became a reality in 1963. But _Parade's_ reach was entirely a function of Sunday newspaper subscriptions, and when those started their long decline, the magazine went with them. Conde Nast parent Advance Publications sold _Parade_ in 2014. The Arena Group picked it up in 2022 and killed the print edition months later. The last physical copy hit doorsteps on Nov. 13, 2022. A brief run as an e-magazine ended in December 2023. Today _Parade_ [lives on as a website](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykj71uwyAYAJ8GtkT8GcjA0CVbunZEX-EjpsLGwl9t9e2r9BU6n-6k-3jEB9RW1-c7LBio9LjiuTckwhGP2huulEZdMPdzhZ36N5XRoxLKXoS_SBshUT0wGuA5FESFmmOQzlvvjL0JPgc32aRtct7dJgWyTFboT3ETpRgNEjyv4dUTXlophDH-amGSKqPSerJYMDEjMFfq4_rV60ozlvbTDxzX1Bfewky07Uy_MXVn6r7BgIwvxNSdj5C3s7ZWd-uYEc8FavvT6J-3R1C_AQAA__8t4mk8) and email newsletter featuring recipes, listicles, and celebrity slideshows. This product is not intended to diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any disease. | Whatever happened to Parade Magazine? If you grew up in a household that got the Sunday paper, you knew Parade. It was right there between the comics and the coupons, a slim, glossy magazine you never subscribed to but never missed. And for decades, it was one of the most widely read publications. Marshall Field III, the department store heir, launched Parade in 1941 as a picture-heavy Sunday supplement for his Chicago Sun and a handful of other papers. By the late 1980s, it was tucked inside more than 330 newspapers, boasting a circulation north of 35 million and a readership that topped 80 million. Here's a gallery of Its features became Sunday morning rituals. , the celebrity Q&A column on the inside cover, was written for 33 years by Lloyd Shearer under that pen name, and was arguably the most widely read column in America. The annual which ran for four decades, let you peek at your neighbor's salary alongside Hollywood's. And the , launched in 1963, proved uncannily prophetic--its alumni include Joe Montana, Peyton Manning, and 14 future Heisman Trophy winners. Parade even nudged history. In 1960, editor Jess Gorkin published an open letter to President Dwight Eisenhower and Soviet Premier Nikita Khrushchev, urging a direct crisis phone link, asking, "Must a world be lost for want of a telephone call?" After the Cuban Missile Crisis exposed just how dangerously slow superpower communication was, the Washington-Moscow hotline became a reality in 1963. But Parade's reach was entirely a function of Sunday newspaper subscriptions, and when those started their long decline, the magazine went with them. Conde Nast parent Advance Publications sold Parade in 2014. The Arena Group picked it up in 2022 and killed the print edition months later. The last physical copy hit doorsteps on Nov. 13, 2022. A brief run as an e-magazine ended in December 2023. Today Parade and email newsletter featuring recipes, listicles, and celebrity slideshows. The name is the same. Everything else that made it a Sunday morning institution is gone. Were you a regular reader of Parade, and did you have a favorite feature?
